argument_summary: The admissible record supports only a narrowed certification position: certification is defensible if treated as conditional on explicit pre-launch model-card disclosure of the health-plan benefits support limitation. Aggregate readiness, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and a 3% rollout with rollback and monitoring support launch prudence, but they do not cure the exposed below-target named use case. The correct reading is not that rollout controls substitute for governance requirements; it is that they support deployment risk management while disclosure satisfies the remaining policy condition for an exposed material limitation.
claims_about_policy: The policy predicate is straightforward: when a named launch use case has a material limitation and remains exposed, rollout controls and monitoring do not remove disclosure duties unless the exposure is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance. The admissible evidence shows no approved risk acceptance covering the exposed health-plan benefits support segment, so the supportable path is certification conditioned on explicit model-card disclosure, consistent with both the release policy and public model-card guidance.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost argument is needed to justify this position. The defense relies on a narrower compliance reading from the admissible record, not on urgency or launch-pressure considerations.
concessions: The health-plan benefits support segment remains below target on benefits-eligibility explanation and is still exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The available risk acceptance is unsigned and does not address the exposed health-plan benefits support segment.
There is no admissible evidence that the required disclosure has already been completed or approved.
An unconditional reading of `certify_model` would overstate what the admissible evidence supports.
